summary: Defines a new IANA registry for the values of the SIP Priority header field and updates RFC 3261 accordingly. This gives a central place to record those values.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 6878 creates an IANA registry for values of SIP's Priority header. It records four existing values and requires IETF Review for new registrations.

subtitle: An IANA registry for the values of SIP's Priority header field.

tldr.problem: The SIP Priority header allowed new values, but no registry had been established to record them.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC creates a Priority Header Field Values sub-registry with four initial values and an IETF Review registration policy.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6878 updates RFC 3261 by providing a controlled way to register SIP Priority values.

today: RFC 6878 is a Proposed Standard from March 2013 and updates RFC 3261.

sections.title: Why the Registry Was Needed
sections.content:
The SIP Priority header field was defined in RFC 3261 in a way that allowed values beyond those originally specified. However, no registry had been set up to keep track of additional values.

RFC 6878 updates RFC 3261 by defining a registry for values of that header field.
sections.plainLanguage: SIP's Priority header could have new values, but there was no official list of them. This RFC creates that list.

sections.title: Initial Values and Registration Policy
sections.content:
The new sub-registry, named Priority Header Field Values, is part of the Session Initiation Protocol (SIP) Parameters registry page. Its initial values are non-urgent, normal, urgent, and emergency, each referenced to RFC 3261.

New values require IETF Review because their semantics could have architectural impact. The RFC advises people considering a new value to consider whether SIP Resource-Priority or another protocol is more appropriate.
sections.plainLanguage: The registry starts with four values: non-urgent, normal, urgent, and emergency. Adding another value needs IETF Review because it could affect how SIP is designed.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that this document has no impact on SIP security. Its purpose is administrative: it creates a registry and defines the policy for adding values.
sections.plainLanguage: This document organizes the header's values. The RFC says it does not affect SIP security.
